Boundary of thick amphibolite with grey felsic orthogneiss. Transposed granitic pegmatites near the boundary within the amphibolite show reddening alteration. Mag is v. common in several such pegmatites and occurs as an accessory mineral in the adjace

5m wide lense of rusty weathered BIF. Lenses occur in strongly foliated dark grey g-chl schist on the E side of this bay. Med-coarse gr act-alb rocks (sill?) outcrop at the boundary with these schists.
See notebook #3 for details - complex section through range of amph facies marine metaseds incl g-chl schists, BIF, chert, tuffs. basalt.

Boundary bw felsic orthogneiss and amphibolite, locally g-bearing - the same wide amphibolite mapped near Manermiut (jho03-310). Within the amphibolite near the boundary is a 30m wide layer of g-mu-bearing quartzite, sample 459418 taken here.
Amphibolite layer with nearby north and south boundaries with felsic orthogneiss. Orthogneiss is very reddened anbd altered here. Ep common along brittle shears both in orthogneiss and amphibolite.

Dominanted by bt-rich layers with porphyroblastic deep pink-red g (<3cm). Foliation // felsic layers common (q-pl). G wrapped by bt, often with felsic strain shadows, commonly and consistently showing sinistral asymmetry.

Lineation defined by q rodding and fibrous sil alignment. The sil-rich rocks are often only sil-q with minor bt.

G-sil-bt-bearing paragneiss with compositional layering of q-rich and bt-rich thin layers. Main gneissosity folded in cm to m-scale folds prevalent here and on adjacent large island to the N. Sil folded in cm-scale folds of same generation.
Similar to jho03-062 though poorer in mu and g-bearing. Folds of q-rich layers still common, though foliation is more distinct, as is bt elongation lineation.
Brown weathered shaley layers of g-bt-sil-(ky?)-pl-q schist interlayered with more q-rich sil-absent layers. Bt defines mineral lineation.
The fine-gnd light grey gneiss here corresponds to Adam's qtz-diorite E of here, which probably was an orthogneiss. But this again looks more like a felsic paragneiss to me.
